"""The verdict contract: one shape of answer for all nine requirement checks.

A check is a function `run(path: Path) -> Verdict`. It never raises for a trace it
cannot evaluate and it never returns a bare boolean. Three outcomes exist:

    PASS          the measurand was observed in scope and respects the bound
    FAIL          the measurand was observed in scope and violates the bound
    INCONCLUSIVE  the measurand could not be observed, with the reason stated

INCONCLUSIVE is not a soft pass. A check that cannot see its measurand -- missing
channel, truncated collision run, too few in-scope samples, or a premise that never
occurs in the trace -- says so, and the harness must treat it as no evidence.

Every bound, window, tolerance and minimum sample count lives in the `CheckSpec`
declared at the top of each check module, next to the requirement id and the
requirement's own `verification_tag`. Nothing quantitative is written inline in the
evaluation logic.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import StrEnum
from pathlib import Path


class Status(StrEnum):
    """The three verdicts. `INCONCLUSIVE` never means `PASS`."""

    PASS = "PASS"
    FAIL = "FAIL"
    INCONCLUSIVE = "INCONCLUSIVE"


class Comparison(StrEnum):
    """How the measured value is compared with the bound, as the requirement words it."""

    AT_MOST = "<="  # "not more than", "within"
    AT_LEAST = ">="  # "not less than"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Verdict:
    """The structured answer. `as_dict()` is the machine-readable form for a harness."""

    test_case_id: str
    requirement_id: str
    verification_tag: str
    title: str
    trace: str
    status: Status
    measured: float | None
    bound: float | None
    comparison: Comparison | None
    tolerance: float
    unit: str
    window: str
    samples_in_scope: int
    scope: str
    signals: tuple[str, ...]
    reason: str
    notes: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)

    @property
    def margin(self) -> float | None:
        """Signed distance to the bound: positive means compliant, negative means violated."""
        if self.measured is None or self.bound is None:
            return None
        if self.comparison is Comparison.AT_LEAST:
            return self.measured - self.bound
        return self.bound - self.measured

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Flat JSON-serialisable mapping. Enums render as their strings."""
        return {
            "test_case_id": self.test_case_id,
            "requirement_id": self.requirement_id,
            "verification_tag": self.verification_tag,
            "title": self.title,
            "trace": self.trace,
            "status": str(self.status),
            "measured": self.measured,
            "bound": self.bound,
            "comparison": str(self.comparison) if self.comparison else None,
            "tolerance": self.tolerance,
            "unit": self.unit,
            "window": self.window,
            "samples_in_scope": self.samples_in_scope,
            "scope": self.scope,
            "signals": list(self.signals),
            "margin": self.margin,
            "reason": self.reason,
            "notes": list(self.notes),
        }


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CheckSpec:
    """Everything quantitative about one check, declared once at the top of its module.

    `verification_tag` is copied verbatim from the requirement record in
    `Reqs/requirements/*.yaml`. A tag of `UNVERIFIED-2018` means the bound below is an
    engineering assumption carried from an older edition of ISO 15622, not a value read
    from the 2018 edition, and a reviewer must see that before trusting a FAIL.
    """

    test_case_id: str
    requirement_id: str
    verification_tag: str
    title: str
    bound: float
    comparison: Comparison
    unit: str
    window: str
    scope: str
    signals: tuple[str, ...]
    min_samples: int
    tolerance: float = 0.0

    def decide(self, measured: float) -> Status:
        """Compare against the bound, widened by the declared measurement tolerance."""
        if self.comparison is Comparison.AT_LEAST:
            return Status.PASS if measured >= self.bound - self.tolerance else Status.FAIL
        return Status.PASS if measured <= self.bound + self.tolerance else Status.FAIL

    def verdict(
        self,
        path: Path,
        *,
        measured: float,
        samples_in_scope: int,
        reason: str,
        notes: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    ) -> Verdict:
        """A PASS or FAIL verdict for a measurand that was actually observed."""
        return Verdict(
            test_case_id=self.test_case_id,
            requirement_id=self.requirement_id,
            verification_tag=self.verification_tag,
            title=self.title,
            trace=str(path),
            status=self.decide(measured),
            measured=measured,
            bound=self.bound,
            comparison=self.comparison,
            tolerance=self.tolerance,
            unit=self.unit,
            window=self.window,
            samples_in_scope=samples_in_scope,
            scope=self.scope,
            signals=self.signals,
            reason=reason,
            notes=notes,
        )

    def inconclusive(
        self,
        path: Path,
        reason: str,
        *,
        samples_in_scope: int = 0,
        notes: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    ) -> Verdict:
        """No measurement was possible. `measured` stays None so nothing can read a zero."""
        return Verdict(
            test_case_id=self.test_case_id,
            requirement_id=self.requirement_id,
            verification_tag=self.verification_tag,
            title=self.title,
            trace=str(path),
            status=Status.INCONCLUSIVE,
            measured=None,
            bound=self.bound,
            comparison=self.comparison,
            tolerance=self.tolerance,
            unit=self.unit,
            window=self.window,
            samples_in_scope=samples_in_scope,
            scope=self.scope,
            signals=self.signals,
            reason=reason,
            notes=notes,
        )

    def too_few_samples(self, path: Path, found: int) -> Verdict:
        """Standard wording for the "in scope but not enough of it" case."""
        return self.inconclusive(
            path,
            f"only {found} {self.scope} in this trace, and this check needs at least "
            f"{self.min_samples}; the trace does not exercise the requirement",
            samples_in_scope=found,
        )

"""Shared helper for all nine checks: open a trace, align rasters, gate, and average.

Everything in this module is here because at least two checks need it. Nothing here knows
a requirement threshold.

Raster alignment
----------------
The catalogue writes four channel groups at three different rates (spec section 6.3):
`PT_CAN_100Hz`, `RADAR_OBJ_50Hz`, `ACC_HMI_10Hz`, plus the non-bus `SIM_REF_100Hz`
ground-truth group, which no check may read. A requirement such as PRF-020 mixes a 100 Hz
physical channel with a 10 Hz state channel, so the two must be put on one grid first.

The rule used everywhere: pick one group's timestamps as the common grid (usually the
100 Hz `PT_CAN_100Hz` grid, the finest bus raster) and carry every other channel onto it
by **zero-order hold** -- each sample is held until the next one arrives, which is what a
real bus receiver does with a frame. Enums and flags are never interpolated, because a
linear blend of `Active-Follow` and `Active-Hold` is not a state. The consequence a check
must report is quantisation: a state change seen on the 10 Hz raster is known only to
within one 100 ms period, so a latency measured against a 10 Hz channel carries up to
100 ms of one-sided uncertainty.

Samples are widened to float64 on read. The file stores float32 and uint8 (spec 6.4);
widening keeps a 200-sample moving average from accumulating float32 rounding error.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import xml.etree.ElementTree as ElementTree
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import IntEnum
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from asammdf import MDF

from TestImpl.verdict import CheckSpec, Verdict

# --- names and group identities, read from a real file, not assumed -------------------

MASTER_CHANNEL_NAME = "time"

GROUP_PT_CAN_100HZ = "PT_CAN_100Hz"
GROUP_RADAR_OBJ_50HZ = "RADAR_OBJ_50Hz"
GROUP_ACC_HMI_10HZ = "ACC_HMI_10Hz"
GROUP_SIM_REF_100HZ = "SIM_REF_100Hz"

#: Ground truth. Excluded by design (spec 6.3): a real vehicle log has no such group, so a
#: check that read it would not be verifying anything a real trace could support.
FORBIDDEN_GROUP = GROUP_SIM_REF_100HZ

#: A driver pedal is released when it reads exactly zero. The plant prescribes pedal
#: position, so there is no sensor noise to threshold away.
PEDAL_RELEASED_PCT = 0.0

#: m/s to km/h. Definitionally exact, and the only kind of literal the project's
#: no-magic-numbers directive allows in code.
KPH_PER_MPS = 3.6


class AccStatus(IntEnum):
    """`ACC_Status` enum, verbatim from the channel comment in the MF4.

    "ACC state: 0=Off,1=Standby,2=Active-Cruise,3=Active-Follow,4=Active-Hold,
    5=Driver-Override,6=Degraded/Fault."
    """

    OFF = 0
    STANDBY = 1
    ACTIVE_CRUISE = 2
    ACTIVE_FOLLOW = 3
    ACTIVE_HOLD = 4
    DRIVER_OVERRIDE = 5
    DEGRADED_FAULT = 6


class RadarStatus(IntEnum):
    """`Rdr_Sts_Enum` enum, verbatim from the channel comment in the MF4.

    "Sensor health: 0=OK, 1=degraded, 2=blocked/fault. A sensor_dropout fault reports
    blocked; a sensor_bias fault is undetected and deliberately leaves this at OK."
    """

    OK = 0
    DEGRADED = 1
    BLOCKED = 2


#: The two states in which the ACC controls speed automatically. Used by the requirements
#: whose `system_states` name Active-Cruise and Active-Follow.
ACTIVE_CONTROL_STATES = (AccStatus.ACTIVE_CRUISE, AccStatus.ACTIVE_FOLLOW)

#: The three states in which automatic brake control can be commanded.
ACTIVE_STATES_WITH_HOLD = (
    AccStatus.ACTIVE_CRUISE,
    AccStatus.ACTIVE_FOLLOW,
    AccStatus.ACTIVE_HOLD,
)


class TraceError(Exception):
    """The trace cannot be used for this check. Always becomes an INCONCLUSIVE verdict."""


class MissingSignalError(TraceError):
    """A channel the check needs is not in the file."""

    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"channel {name!r} is not present in the file")
        self.name = name


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Channel:
    """One channel as read from the file: its own timestamps, its samples, its unit."""

    name: str
    unit: str
    time: np.ndarray
    samples: np.ndarray


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LatencyMeasurement:
    """Time from a reference instant to the first sample that satisfies some condition.

    Exists to keep the three latency checks (hold entry, brake-lamp illumination, fault entry)
    honest about the case where the awaited event simply never happens. When it does not, the
    latency is only a *lower bound* -- the time from the reference instant to the end of the
    trace -- and that is enough to decide the verdict only if the bound has already been
    exceeded. A trace that stops 0.4 s after a standstill cannot show whether a 3 s deadline
    was met, and `is_conclusive()` says so instead of returning 0.4 s as a PASS.
    """

    reference_t: float
    reached_t: float | None
    trace_end_t: float

    @property
    def is_censored(self) -> bool:
        """True when the awaited condition never occurred in the trace."""
        return self.reached_t is None

    @property
    def latency_s(self) -> float:
        """Measured latency, or its lower bound when the measurement is censored.

        May be negative: a system that reacts before the reference instant is early, and that
        is reported rather than clamped, because clamping hides the observation.
        """
        end = self.trace_end_t if self.reached_t is None else self.reached_t
        return end - self.reference_t

    def is_conclusive(self, limit_s: float) -> bool:
        """Whether this measurement can decide a verdict against `limit_s`."""
        return not self.is_censored or self.latency_s > limit_s


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Episode:
    """A contiguous run of samples for which some condition held."""

    first_index: int
    last_index: int
    t_start: float
    t_end: float

    @property
    def duration_s(self) -> float:
        """Time from the first sample of the episode to its last sample."""
        return self.t_end - self.t_start


class Trace:
    """One MF4 file, plus the run metadata the generator embedded in its header.

    Channel names are unique across the bus groups in this catalogue (only the per-group
    master `time` repeats), so channels are fetched by name alone.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        self.path = Path(path)
        try:
            self._mdf = MDF(self.path)
        except Exception as exc:
            raise TraceError(f"asammdf could not open the file: {exc}") from exc
        self.properties = _read_header_properties(self._mdf)
        self._channels: dict[str, Channel] = {}
        self._grids: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

    # --- run metadata -----------------------------------------------------------------

    @property
    def run_id(self) -> str:
        """Generator run id, e.g. `lead_brake_ccrb_4mps2__v130__d3c693ca7316`."""
        return self.properties.get("run_id", self.path.stem)

    @property
    def scenario_name(self) -> str:
        """Scenario the run came from, e.g. `lead_brake_ccrb_4mps2`."""
        return self.properties.get("scenario_name", "")

    @property
    def is_collision_run(self) -> bool:
        """True when the run ended at contact, which means the file is truncated.

        Three of the 37 catalogue runs are truncated this way. Being shorter is by design,
        not corruption -- but a truncated trace is not valid evidence about the behaviour
        these requirements describe, so every check reports INCONCLUSIVE on it rather than
        guessing from the fragment that was written.
        """
        return self.properties.get("collision", "false").lower() == "true"

    @property
    def collision_t_s(self) -> float | None:
        """Time of contact, when there was one."""
        raw = self.properties.get("collision_t_s", "")
        return float(raw) if raw else None

    # --- channels and grids -----------------------------------------------------------

    def has(self, name: str) -> bool:
        """Whether a channel of this name exists in the file."""
        return any(
            channel.name == name for group in self._mdf.groups for channel in group.channels
        )

    def channel(self, name: str) -> Channel:
        """Fetch a channel with its unit and its own timestamps. Cached per trace."""
        if name in self._channels:
            return self._channels[name]
        if not self.has(name):
            raise MissingSignalError(name)
        signal = self._mdf.get(name)
        channel = Channel(
            name=name,
            unit=str(signal.unit),
            time=np.asarray(signal.timestamps, dtype=float),
            samples=np.asarray(signal.samples, dtype=float),
        )
        self._channels[name] = channel
        return channel

    def grid(self, group_name: str) -> np.ndarray:
        """Timestamps of a channel group, to be used as a common grid.

        Taken from the group's first data channel rather than from a hard-coded signal
        name, so the grid does not depend on which signal a check happens to want.
        """
        if group_name == FORBIDDEN_GROUP:
            raise TraceError(
                f"{FORBIDDEN_GROUP} is simulator ground truth and is excluded from "
                "requirement checking by design (spec 6.3)"
            )
        if group_name in self._grids:
            return self._grids[group_name]
        for group in self._mdf.groups:
            if group.channel_group.acq_name != group_name:
                continue
            for channel in group.channels:
                if channel.name != MASTER_CHANNEL_NAME:
                    self._grids[group_name] = self.channel(channel.name).time
                    return self._grids[group_name]
        raise TraceError(f"channel group {group_name!r} is not present in the file")

    def on_grid(self, name: str, t_grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """A channel's samples carried onto `t_grid` by zero-order hold.

        Each source sample is held until the next one arrives. Grid samples before the
        channel's first timestamp hold that first sample; in this catalogue every group
        starts at t = 0, so that clamp does not trigger in practice.
        """
        channel = self.channel(name)
        return hold_onto(channel.time, channel.samples, t_grid)

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Release the file handle."""
        self._mdf.close()

    def __enter__(self) -> Trace:
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
        self.close()


def open_trace(path: Path) -> Trace:
    """Open an MF4 trace. Raises `TraceError` if it cannot be read."""
    return Trace(path)


def _read_header_properties(mdf: MDF) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Parse the `common_properties` block the generator wrote into the MF4 header.

    Self-contained on purpose: the same fields are in `Data/manifest.csv` and in the
    `.meta.json` sidecar, but a check must work on a single file a user uploaded with no
    sidecar next to it.
    """
    comment = getattr(mdf.header, "comment", "") or ""
    if not comment.strip().startswith("<"):
        return {}
    try:
        root = ElementTree.fromstring(comment)
    except ElementTree.ParseError:
        return {}
    return {
        element.get("name", ""): (element.text or "").strip()
        for element in root.findall("./common_properties/e")
    }


# --- alignment, gating, reduction -----------------------------------------------------


def hold_onto(t_source: np.ndarray, samples: np.ndarray, t_grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Zero-order hold resample of `samples` from `t_source` onto `t_grid`."""
    indices = np.searchsorted(t_source, t_grid, side="right") - 1
    return samples[np.clip(indices, 0, samples.size - 1)]


def grid_step_s(t_grid: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Sample period of a uniform grid, taken as the median difference."""
    if t_grid.size < 2:
        raise TraceError("the common grid has fewer than two samples")
    return float(np.median(np.diff(t_grid)))


def window_length_samples(t_grid: np.ndarray, window_s: float) -> int:
    """How many samples of `t_grid` a window of `window_s` seconds spans."""
    return int(round(window_s / grid_step_s(t_grid)))


def build_gate(
    trace: Trace,
    t_grid: np.ndarray,
    allowed_states: Sequence[int],
    *,
    require_brake_released: bool = True,
    require_accel_released: bool = False,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """The state and pedal gate, on `t_grid`.

    Gating is not optional. `VehAccel_mps2` is the *achieved* acceleration and includes
    whatever the driver does: in `driver_override_brake` it reaches 3.85 m/s^2 of
    deceleration while `BrkReq_mps2` is exactly 0, because that is the driver braking and
    not the ACC. Restricting to the requirement's own `system_states` and to a released
    brake pedal drops that run's worst 2 s average from 3.85 to 0.03 m/s^2. Without the
    gate a check reports failures the ACC never caused.
    """
    status = trace.on_grid("ACC_Status", t_grid)
    gate = np.isin(status, np.asarray(allowed_states, dtype=float))
    if require_brake_released:
        gate &= trace.on_grid("DrvBrkPedal_Pct", t_grid) <= PEDAL_RELEASED_PCT
    if require_accel_released:
        gate &= trace.on_grid("DrvAccPedal_Pct", t_grid) <= PEDAL_RELEASED_PCT
    return gate


def masked_moving_average(
    values: np.ndarray, gate: np.ndarray, window_samples: int
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Mean of `values` over every window of `window_samples` lying fully inside `gate`.

    Returns `(start_indices, means)` for the admitted windows only.

    A window that straddles the edge of the gated region is dropped, not partially
    averaged. Averaging it would quietly mix in samples from outside the requirement's
    scope -- for a 2 s window at 100 Hz that is up to 199 out-of-scope samples diluting
    one in-scope sample, which can turn a real violation into a pass or the reverse.
    """
    count = int(window_samples)
    if count <= 0 or values.size < count:
        return np.empty(0, dtype=int), np.empty(0, dtype=float)
    value_sum = np.concatenate(([0.0], np.cumsum(values, dtype=float)))
    gate_sum = np.concatenate(([0], np.cumsum(gate.astype(np.int64))))
    starts = np.arange(values.size - count + 1)
    fully_inside = (gate_sum[starts + count] - gate_sum[starts]) == count
    starts = starts[fully_inside]
    means = (value_sum[starts + count] - value_sum[starts]) / count
    return starts, means


def rising_edges(flag: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Indices where a 0/1 flag becomes asserted. The first sample counts if it is 1."""
    asserted = flag > 0.5
    previous = np.concatenate(([False], asserted[:-1]))
    return np.flatnonzero(asserted & ~previous)


def find_episodes(condition: np.ndarray, t_grid: np.ndarray) -> list[Episode]:
    """Every contiguous run of samples for which `condition` is True."""
    held = np.asarray(condition, dtype=bool)
    if not held.any():
        return []
    previous = np.concatenate(([False], held[:-1]))
    following = np.concatenate((held[1:], [False]))
    starts = np.flatnonzero(held & ~previous)
    ends = np.flatnonzero(held & ~following)
    return [
        Episode(int(first), int(last), float(t_grid[first]), float(t_grid[last]))
        for first, last in zip(starts, ends, strict=True)
    ]


def first_index_where(condition: np.ndarray, at_or_after: int) -> int | None:
    """Index of the first True at or after `at_or_after`, or None if there is none."""
    hits = np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(condition, dtype=bool)[at_or_after:])
    return int(hits[0]) + at_or_after if hits.size else None


def measure_latency(
    t_grid: np.ndarray, condition: np.ndarray, reference_t: float, search_from: int
) -> LatencyMeasurement:
    """Latency from `reference_t` to the first sample at or after `search_from` satisfying it.

    `reference_t` and `search_from` are separate on purpose. ACC-SYS-SAF-021 measures from a
    detection instant 500 ms into a sensor dropout but has to start searching at the beginning
    of the dropout, so that a system reacting before the debounce elapses is seen and reported
    as early rather than missed.
    """
    hit = first_index_where(condition, search_from)
    return LatencyMeasurement(
        reference_t=reference_t,
        reached_t=None if hit is None else float(t_grid[hit]),
        trace_end_t=float(t_grid[-1]),
    )


def status_name(value: float) -> str:
    """Human name for an `ACC_Status` sample, or the raw number if it is not a known state."""
    try:
        return AccStatus(int(value)).name
    except ValueError:
        return f"unknown({int(value)})"


def require_channels(trace: Trace, names: Iterable[str]) -> None:
    """Raise `MissingSignalError` for the first channel that is absent.

    Called before any measurement, so that a file lacking a measurand reports
    INCONCLUSIVE naming the channel instead of measuring whatever it does contain.
    """
    for name in names:
        if not trace.has(name):
            raise MissingSignalError(name)


def run_check(spec: CheckSpec, path: Path, evaluate: Callable[[Trace], Verdict]) -> Verdict:
    """Uniform wrapper: open the trace, apply the shared INCONCLUSIVE rules, evaluate.

    Every check module's `run()` is this call and nothing else, so all nine behave
    identically on an unreadable file, a missing channel or a truncated collision run.
    """
    try:
        with open_trace(path) as trace:
            if trace.is_collision_run:
                contact = trace.collision_t_s
                moment = f"{contact:.2f} s" if contact is not None else "an unrecorded time"
                return spec.inconclusive(
                    path,
                    f"run {trace.run_id} ended at a collision at t = {moment} and the file is "
                    "truncated there, so it is not valid evidence for this requirement",
                )
            require_channels(trace, spec.signals)
            return evaluate(trace)
    except TraceError as exc:
        return spec.inconclusive(path, str(exc))

TC-ACC-SYS-PRF-001 -- minimum time gap of 0,8 s in Active-Follow.

Requirement ACC-SYS-PRF-001: "While the ACC system is in the Active-Follow state under
steady-state conditions, the ACC system shall maintain a time gap to the target vehicle of
not less than 0,8 s at every subject vehicle speed within the operating speed range."

The measured time gap is `Trgt_Dist_m / v_ego`, the clearance divided by the subject
vehicle's own speed -- the definition the spacing law uses (spec 2.3).

"Steady-state conditions" is the requirement's own qualifier and it has to be given an
observable meaning, because the gap is legitimately smaller than tau during a transient
while the controller is still closing on the target. This check calls a sample steady when
all of the following hold, and reports the definition with the verdict:

    * the annunciated state is Active-Follow,
    * the primary target is valid and classified in-lane,
    * both driver pedals are released,
    * the achieved acceleration is small -- the vehicle is not still converging,
    * the relative speed to the target is small -- the gap is settled, not closing.

Speeds below a floor are excluded only to keep the division well conditioned. That is not a
requirement bound: below `c_min / tau` the spacing law is clearance-limited, which makes the
*measured* time gap larger, so no exclusion there can hide a violation.

    python -m TestImpl.tc_acc_sys_prf_001 Data/follow_steady_timegap/<run>__tau08__*.mf4

    python -m TestImpl.tc_acc_sys_prf_001 Data/follow_steady_timegap/<run>__tau08__*.mf4
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from TestImpl.report import single_trace_main
from TestImpl.trace import (
    GROUP_PT_CAN_100HZ,
    KPH_PER_MPS,
    PEDAL_RELEASED_PCT,
    AccStatus,
    Trace,
    run_check,
)
from TestImpl.verdict import CheckSpec, Comparison, Status, Verdict

# --- declared values. Nothing quantitative appears below this block. ------------------

#: ACC-SYS-PRF-001, verification_tag VERIFIED-PRIMARY. ISO 15622:2018 cl. 6.2.3.1 states
#: that the minimum selectable time gap for following control under steady-state conditions
#: shall be >= 0,8 s for all speeds. Read from the publisher-hosted 2018 preview, which does
#: reach this clause. The value changed between editions -- the 2002 first edition required
#: 1 s -- so the edition matters.
MIN_TIME_GAP_S = 0.8

#: No tolerance. The clearance quantum is 0.05 m, which at 25 m/s is 0.002 s of time gap,
#: three orders below the bound; nothing needs widening.
MEASUREMENT_TOLERANCE_S = 0.0

#: Steady-state definition. Both are PROJECT-CHOICE measurement parameters of this test, not
#: requirement values: the requirement says "under steady-state conditions" and defines no
#: numbers. Loose enough to admit a real following run, tight enough to exclude the closing
#: transient in which a smaller gap is expected and permitted.
STEADY_ACCEL_EPS_MPS2 = 0.3
STEADY_REL_SPEED_EPS_MPS = 0.5

#: Division floor on ego speed, in m/s. Numerical conditioning only -- see the module
#: docstring for why excluding low speed cannot mask a violation.
MIN_EGO_SPEED_MPS = 1.0

#: One second of 100 Hz samples. A shorter window is a transient, not a steady state.
MIN_SAMPLES = 100

CHECK = CheckSpec(
    test_case_id="TC-ACC-SYS-PRF-001",
    requirement_id="ACC-SYS-PRF-001",
    verification_tag="VERIFIED-PRIMARY",
    title="Minimum selectable time gap",
    bound=MIN_TIME_GAP_S,
    comparison=Comparison.AT_LEAST,
    unit="s",
    window="instantaneous, per steady-state sample",
    scope="steady-state Active-Follow samples on the 100 Hz grid",
    signals=(
        "Trgt_Dist_m",
        "VehSpd_Kph",
        "Trgt_RelSpd_mps",
        "Trgt_Valid_Flg",
        "Trgt_InLane_Flg",
        "VehAccel_mps2",
        "ACC_Status",
        "ACC_TimeGapSet_s",
        "DrvBrkPedal_Pct",
        "DrvAccPedal_Pct",
    ),
    min_samples=MIN_SAMPLES,
    tolerance=MEASUREMENT_TOLERANCE_S,
)


def evaluate(trace: Trace) -> Verdict:
    """Smallest steady-state time gap the ACC held while following."""
    t_grid = trace.grid(GROUP_PT_CAN_100HZ)
    ego_speed_mps = trace.on_grid("VehSpd_Kph", t_grid) / KPH_PER_MPS
    clearance_m = trace.on_grid("Trgt_Dist_m", t_grid)
    steady = _steady_state_mask(trace, t_grid, ego_speed_mps)
    if int(steady.sum()) < MIN_SAMPLES:
        return CHECK.too_few_samples(trace.path, int(steady.sum()))

    time_gap_s = clearance_m / np.where(steady, ego_speed_mps, 1.0)
    worst = float(time_gap_s[steady].min())
    worst_index = int(np.flatnonzero(steady)[np.argmin(time_gap_s[steady])])
    selected_tau_s = float(trace.on_grid("ACC_TimeGapSet_s", t_grid)[worst_index])
    outcome = "respects" if CHECK.decide(worst) is Status.PASS else "is below"

    return CHECK.verdict(
        trace.path,
        measured=worst,
        samples_in_scope=int(steady.sum()),
        reason=(
            f"the smallest steady-state time gap was {worst:.3f} s, at t = "
            f"{t_grid[worst_index]:.2f} s with {clearance_m[worst_index]:.2f} m of clearance at "
            f"{ego_speed_mps[worst_index] * KPH_PER_MPS:.1f} km/h and tau set to "
            f"{selected_tau_s:.1f} s; that {outcome} the {MIN_TIME_GAP_S:.1f} s floor"
        ),
        notes=_notes(trace, t_grid, steady),
    )


def _steady_state_mask(trace: Trace, t_grid: np.ndarray, ego_speed_mps: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Where the run is genuinely following at a settled gap. See the module docstring."""
    status = trace.on_grid("ACC_Status", t_grid)
    return (
        (status == AccStatus.ACTIVE_FOLLOW)
        & (trace.on_grid("Trgt_Valid_Flg", t_grid) > 0.5)
        & (trace.on_grid("Trgt_InLane_Flg", t_grid) > 0.5)
        & (trace.on_grid("DrvBrkPedal_Pct", t_grid) <= PEDAL_RELEASED_PCT)
        & (trace.on_grid("DrvAccPedal_Pct", t_grid) <= PEDAL_RELEASED_PCT)
        & (np.abs(trace.on_grid("VehAccel_mps2", t_grid)) <= STEADY_ACCEL_EPS_MPS2)
        & (np.abs(trace.on_grid("Trgt_RelSpd_mps", t_grid)) <= STEADY_REL_SPEED_EPS_MPS)
        & (ego_speed_mps >= MIN_EGO_SPEED_MPS)
    )


def _notes(trace: Trace, t_grid: np.ndarray, steady: np.ndarray) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The steady-state definition, and which tau settings were actually exercised."""
    tau_settings = np.unique(trace.on_grid("ACC_TimeGapSet_s", t_grid)[steady])
    exercised = ", ".join(f"{value:.1f}" for value in tau_settings)
    return (
        f"steady state means Active-Follow with a valid in-lane target, pedals released, "
        f"|VehAccel_mps2| <= {STEADY_ACCEL_EPS_MPS2} m/s^2 and |Trgt_RelSpd_mps| <= "
        f"{STEADY_REL_SPEED_EPS_MPS} m/s; {int(steady.sum())} of {steady.size} samples of the "
        f"100 Hz grid qualified",
        f"tau setting(s) exercised in scope: {exercised} s. The requirement is on the gap the "
        f"system actually holds, so a run whose tau is set well above 0.8 s cannot challenge "
        f"the floor -- follow_steady_timegap__tau08 is the run that can",
        "the 50 Hz clearance and relative speed and the 10 Hz state and tau are carried onto "
        "the 100 Hz speed grid by zero-order hold",
    )


def run(path: Path) -> Verdict:
    """Evaluate one MF4 trace against ACC-SYS-PRF-001."""
    return run_check(CHECK, path, evaluate)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run this single check from the command line."""
    return single_trace_main(__name__, run, argv)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
source.verdict.py:
"""The verdict contract: one shape of answer for all nine requirement checks.

A check is a function `run(path: Path) -> Verdict`. It never raises for a trace it
cannot evaluate and it never returns a bare boolean. Three outcomes exist:

    PASS          the measurand was observed in scope and respects the bound
    FAIL          the measurand was observed in scope and violates the bound
    INCONCLUSIVE  the measurand could not be observed, with the reason stated

INCONCLUSIVE is not a soft pass. A check that cannot see its measurand -- missing
channel, truncated collision run, too few in-scope samples, or a premise that never
occurs in the trace -- says so, and the harness must treat it as no evidence.

Every bound, window, tolerance and minimum sample count lives in the `CheckSpec`
declared at the top of each check module, next to the requirement id and the
requirement's own `verification_tag`. Nothing quantitative is written inline in the
evaluation logic.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import StrEnum
from pathlib import Path


class Status(StrEnum):
    """The three verdicts. `INCONCLUSIVE` never means `PASS`."""

    PASS = "PASS"
    FAIL = "FAIL"
    INCONCLUSIVE = "INCONCLUSIVE"


class Comparison(StrEnum):
    """How the measured value is compared with the bound, as the requirement words it."""

    AT_MOST = "<="  # "not more than", "within"
    AT_LEAST = ">="  # "not less than"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Verdict:
    """The structured answer. `as_dict()` is the machine-readable form for a harness."""

    test_case_id: str
    requirement_id: str
    verification_tag: str
    title: str
    trace: str
    status: Status
    measured: float | None
    bound: float | None
    comparison: Comparison | None
    tolerance: float
    unit: str
    window: str
    samples_in_scope: int
    scope: str
    signals: tuple[str, ...]
    reason: str
    notes: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)

    @property
    def margin(self) -> float | None:
        """Signed distance to the bound: positive means compliant, negative means violated."""
        if self.measured is None or self.bound is None:
            return None
        if self.comparison is Comparison.AT_LEAST:
            return self.measured - self.bound
        return self.bound - self.measured

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Flat JSON-serialisable mapping. Enums render as their strings."""
        return {
            "test_case_id": self.test_case_id,
            "requirement_id": self.requirement_id,
            "verification_tag": self.verification_tag,
            "title": self.title,
            "trace": self.trace,
            "status": str(self.status),
            "measured": self.measured,
            "bound": self.bound,
            "comparison": str(self.comparison) if self.comparison else None,
            "tolerance": self.tolerance,
            "unit": self.unit,
            "window": self.window,
            "samples_in_scope": self.samples_in_scope,
            "scope": self.scope,
            "signals": list(self.signals),
            "margin": self.margin,
            "reason": self.reason,
            "notes": list(self.notes),
        }


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CheckSpec:
    """Everything quantitative about one check, declared once at the top of its module.

    `verification_tag` is copied verbatim from the requirement record in
    `Reqs/requirements/*.yaml`. A tag of `UNVERIFIED-2018` means the bound below is an
    engineering assumption carried from an older edition of ISO 15622, not a value read
    from the 2018 edition, and a reviewer must see that before trusting a FAIL.
    """

    test_case_id: str
    requirement_id: str
    verification_tag: str
    title: str
    bound: float
    comparison: Comparison
    unit: str
    window: str
    scope: str
    signals: tuple[str, ...]
    min_samples: int
    tolerance: float = 0.0

    def decide(self, measured: float) -> Status:
        """Compare against the bound, widened by the declared measurement tolerance."""
        if self.comparison is Comparison.AT_LEAST:
            return Status.PASS if measured >= self.bound - self.tolerance else Status.FAIL
        return Status.PASS if measured <= self.bound + self.tolerance else Status.FAIL

    def verdict(
        self,
        path: Path,
        *,
        measured: float,
        samples_in_scope: int,
        reason: str,
        notes: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    ) -> Verdict:
        """A PASS or FAIL verdict for a measurand that was actually observed."""
        return Verdict(
            test_case_id=self.test_case_id,
            requirement_id=self.requirement_id,
            verification_tag=self.verification_tag,
            title=self.title,
            trace=str(path),
            status=self.decide(measured),
            measured=measured,
            bound=self.bound,
            comparison=self.comparison,
            tolerance=self.tolerance,
            unit=self.unit,
            window=self.window,
            samples_in_scope=samples_in_scope,
            scope=self.scope,
            signals=self.signals,
            reason=reason,
            notes=notes,
        )

    def inconclusive(
        self,
        path: Path,
        reason: str,
        *,
        samples_in_scope: int = 0,
        notes: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    ) -> Verdict:
        """No measurement was possible. `measured` stays None so nothing can read a zero."""
        return Verdict(
            test_case_id=self.test_case_id,
            requirement_id=self.requirement_id,
            verification_tag=self.verification_tag,
            title=self.title,
            trace=str(path),
            status=Status.INCONCLUSIVE,
            measured=None,
            bound=self.bound,
            comparison=self.comparison,
            tolerance=self.tolerance,
            unit=self.unit,
            window=self.window,
            samples_in_scope=samples_in_scope,
            scope=self.scope,
            signals=self.signals,
            reason=reason,
            notes=notes,
        )

    def too_few_samples(self, path: Path, found: int) -> Verdict:
        """Standard wording for the "in scope but not enough of it" case."""
        return self.inconclusive(
            path,
            f"only {found} {self.scope} in this trace, and this check needs at least "
            f"{self.min_samples}; the trace does not exercise the requirement",
            samples_in_scope=found,
        )
source.trace.py:
"""Shared helper for all nine checks: open a trace, align rasters, gate, and average.

Everything in this module is here because at least two checks need it. Nothing here knows
a requirement threshold.

Raster alignment
----------------
The catalogue writes four channel groups at three different rates (spec section 6.3):
`PT_CAN_100Hz`, `RADAR_OBJ_50Hz`, `ACC_HMI_10Hz`, plus the non-bus `SIM_REF_100Hz`
ground-truth group, which no check may read. A requirement such as PRF-020 mixes a 100 Hz
physical channel with a 10 Hz state channel, so the two must be put on one grid first.

The rule used everywhere: pick one group's timestamps as the common grid (usually the
100 Hz `PT_CAN_100Hz` grid, the finest bus raster) and carry every other channel onto it
by **zero-order hold** -- each sample is held until the next one arrives, which is what a
real bus receiver does with a frame. Enums and flags are never interpolated, because a
linear blend of `Active-Follow` and `Active-Hold` is not a state. The consequence a check
must report is quantisation: a state change seen on the 10 Hz raster is known only to
within one 100 ms period, so a latency measured against a 10 Hz channel carries up to
100 ms of one-sided uncertainty.

Samples are widened to float64 on read. The file stores float32 and uint8 (spec 6.4);
widening keeps a 200-sample moving average from accumulating float32 rounding error.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import xml.etree.ElementTree as ElementTree
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import IntEnum
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from asammdf import MDF

from TestImpl.verdict import CheckSpec, Verdict

# --- names and group identities, read from a real file, not assumed -------------------

MASTER_CHANNEL_NAME = "time"

GROUP_PT_CAN_100HZ = "PT_CAN_100Hz"
GROUP_RADAR_OBJ_50HZ = "RADAR_OBJ_50Hz"
GROUP_ACC_HMI_10HZ = "ACC_HMI_10Hz"
GROUP_SIM_REF_100HZ = "SIM_REF_100Hz"

#: Ground truth. Excluded by design (spec 6.3): a real vehicle log has no such group, so a
#: check that read it would not be verifying anything a real trace could support.
FORBIDDEN_GROUP = GROUP_SIM_REF_100HZ

#: A driver pedal is released when it reads exactly zero. The plant prescribes pedal
#: position, so there is no sensor noise to threshold away.
PEDAL_RELEASED_PCT = 0.0

#: m/s to km/h. Definitionally exact, and the only kind of literal the project's
#: no-magic-numbers directive allows in code.
KPH_PER_MPS = 3.6


class AccStatus(IntEnum):
    """`ACC_Status` enum, verbatim from the channel comment in the MF4.

    "ACC state: 0=Off,1=Standby,2=Active-Cruise,3=Active-Follow,4=Active-Hold,
    5=Driver-Override,6=Degraded/Fault."
    """

    OFF = 0
    STANDBY = 1
    ACTIVE_CRUISE = 2
    ACTIVE_FOLLOW = 3
    ACTIVE_HOLD = 4
    DRIVER_OVERRIDE = 5
    DEGRADED_FAULT = 6


class RadarStatus(IntEnum):
    """`Rdr_Sts_Enum` enum, verbatim from the channel comment in the MF4.

    "Sensor health: 0=OK, 1=degraded, 2=blocked/fault. A sensor_dropout fault reports
    blocked; a sensor_bias fault is undetected and deliberately leaves this at OK."
    """

    OK = 0
    DEGRADED = 1
    BLOCKED = 2


#: The two states in which the ACC controls speed automatically. Used by the requirements
#: whose `system_states` name Active-Cruise and Active-Follow.
ACTIVE_CONTROL_STATES = (AccStatus.ACTIVE_CRUISE, AccStatus.ACTIVE_FOLLOW)

#: The three states in which automatic brake control can be commanded.
ACTIVE_STATES_WITH_HOLD = (
    AccStatus.ACTIVE_CRUISE,
    AccStatus.ACTIVE_FOLLOW,
    AccStatus.ACTIVE_HOLD,
)


class TraceError(Exception):
    """The trace cannot be used for this check. Always becomes an INCONCLUSIVE verdict."""


class MissingSignalError(TraceError):
    """A channel the check needs is not in the file."""

    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"channel {name!r} is not present in the file")
        self.name = name


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Channel:
    """One channel as read from the file: its own timestamps, its samples, its unit."""

    name: str
    unit: str
    time: np.ndarray
    samples: np.ndarray


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LatencyMeasurement:
    """Time from a reference instant to the first sample that satisfies some condition.

    Exists to keep the three latency checks (hold entry, brake-lamp illumination, fault entry)
    honest about the case where the awaited event simply never happens. When it does not, the
    latency is only a *lower bound* -- the time from the reference instant to the end of the
    trace -- and that is enough to decide the verdict only if the bound has already been
    exceeded. A trace that stops 0.4 s after a standstill cannot show whether a 3 s deadline
    was met, and `is_conclusive()` says so instead of returning 0.4 s as a PASS.
    """

    reference_t: float
    reached_t: float | None
    trace_end_t: float

    @property
    def is_censored(self) -> bool:
        """True when the awaited condition never occurred in the trace."""
        return self.reached_t is None

    @property
    def latency_s(self) -> float:
        """Measured latency, or its lower bound when the measurement is censored.

        May be negative: a system that reacts before the reference instant is early, and that
        is reported rather than clamped, because clamping hides the observation.
        """
        end = self.trace_end_t if self.reached_t is None else self.reached_t
        return end - self.reference_t

    def is_conclusive(self, limit_s: float) -> bool:
        """Whether this measurement can decide a verdict against `limit_s`."""
        return not self.is_censored or self.latency_s > limit_s


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Episode:
    """A contiguous run of samples for which some condition held."""

    first_index: int
    last_index: int
    t_start: float
    t_end: float

    @property
    def duration_s(self) -> float:
        """Time from the first sample of the episode to its last sample."""
        return self.t_end - self.t_start


class Trace:
    """One MF4 file, plus the run metadata the generator embedded in its header.

    Channel names are unique across the bus groups in this catalogue (only the per-group
    master `time` repeats), so channels are fetched by name alone.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        self.path = Path(path)
        try:
            self._mdf = MDF(self.path)
        except Exception as exc:
            raise TraceError(f"asammdf could not open the file: {exc}") from exc
        self.properties = _read_header_properties(self._mdf)
        self._channels: dict[str, Channel] = {}
        self._grids: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

    # --- run metadata -----------------------------------------------------------------

    @property
    def run_id(self) -> str:
        """Generator run id, e.g. `lead_brake_ccrb_4mps2__v130__d3c693ca7316`."""
        return self.properties.get("run_id", self.path.stem)

    @property
    def scenario_name(self) -> str:
        """Scenario the run came from, e.g. `lead_brake_ccrb_4mps2`."""
        return self.properties.get("scenario_name", "")

    @property
    def is_collision_run(self) -> bool:
        """True when the run ended at contact, which means the file is truncated.

        Three of the 37 catalogue runs are truncated this way. Being shorter is by design,
        not corruption -- but a truncated trace is not valid evidence about the behaviour
        these requirements describe, so every check reports INCONCLUSIVE on it rather than
        guessing from the fragment that was written.
        """
        return self.properties.get("collision", "false").lower() == "true"

    @property
    def collision_t_s(self) -> float | None:
        """Time of contact, when there was one."""
        raw = self.properties.get("collision_t_s", "")
        return float(raw) if raw else None

    # --- channels and grids -----------------------------------------------------------

    def has(self, name: str) -> bool:
        """Whether a channel of this name exists in the file."""
        return any(
            channel.name == name for group in self._mdf.groups for channel in group.channels
        )

    def channel(self, name: str) -> Channel:
        """Fetch a channel with its unit and its own timestamps. Cached per trace."""
        if name in self._channels:
            return self._channels[name]
        if not self.has(name):
            raise MissingSignalError(name)
        signal = self._mdf.get(name)
        channel = Channel(
            name=name,
            unit=str(signal.unit),
            time=np.asarray(signal.timestamps, dtype=float),
            samples=np.asarray(signal.samples, dtype=float),
        )
        self._channels[name] = channel
        return channel

    def grid(self, group_name: str) -> np.ndarray:
        """Timestamps of a channel group, to be used as a common grid.

        Taken from the group's first data channel rather than from a hard-coded signal
        name, so the grid does not depend on which signal a check happens to want.
        """
        if group_name == FORBIDDEN_GROUP:
            raise TraceError(
                f"{FORBIDDEN_GROUP} is simulator ground truth and is excluded from "
                "requirement checking by design (spec 6.3)"
            )
        if group_name in self._grids:
            return self._grids[group_name]
        for group in self._mdf.groups:
            if group.channel_group.acq_name != group_name:
                continue
            for channel in group.channels:
                if channel.name != MASTER_CHANNEL_NAME:
                    self._grids[group_name] = self.channel(channel.name).time
                    return self._grids[group_name]
        raise TraceError(f"channel group {group_name!r} is not present in the file")

    def on_grid(self, name: str, t_grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """A channel's samples carried onto `t_grid` by zero-order hold.

        Each source sample is held until the next one arrives. Grid samples before the
        channel's first timestamp hold that first sample; in this catalogue every group
        starts at t = 0, so that clamp does not trigger in practice.
        """
        channel = self.channel(name)
        return hold_onto(channel.time, channel.samples, t_grid)

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Release the file handle."""
        self._mdf.close()

    def __enter__(self) -> Trace:
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_exc: object) -> None:
        self.close()


def open_trace(path: Path) -> Trace:
    """Open an MF4 trace. Raises `TraceError` if it cannot be read."""
    return Trace(path)


def _read_header_properties(mdf: MDF) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Parse the `common_properties` block the generator wrote into the MF4 header.

    Self-contained on purpose: the same fields are in `Data/manifest.csv` and in the
    `.meta.json` sidecar, but a check must work on a single file a user uploaded with no
    sidecar next to it.
    """
    comment = getattr(mdf.header, "comment", "") or ""
    if not comment.strip().startswith("<"):
        return {}
    try:
        root = ElementTree.fromstring(comment)
    except ElementTree.ParseError:
        return {}
    return {
        element.get("name", ""): (element.text or "").strip()
        for element in root.findall("./common_properties/e")
    }


# --- alignment, gating, reduction -----------------------------------------------------


def hold_onto(t_source: np.ndarray, samples: np.ndarray, t_grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Zero-order hold resample of `samples` from `t_source` onto `t_grid`."""
    indices = np.searchsorted(t_source, t_grid, side="right") - 1
    return samples[np.clip(indices, 0, samples.size - 1)]


def grid_step_s(t_grid: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Sample period of a uniform grid, taken as the median difference."""
    if t_grid.size < 2:
        raise TraceError("the common grid has fewer than two samples")
    return float(np.median(np.diff(t_grid)))


def window_length_samples(t_grid: np.ndarray, window_s: float) -> int:
    """How many samples of `t_grid` a window of `window_s` seconds spans."""
    return int(round(window_s / grid_step_s(t_grid)))


def build_gate(
    trace: Trace,
    t_grid: np.ndarray,
    allowed_states: Sequence[int],
    *,
    require_brake_released: bool = True,
    require_accel_released: bool = False,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """The state and pedal gate, on `t_grid`.

    Gating is not optional. `VehAccel_mps2` is the *achieved* acceleration and includes
    whatever the driver does: in `driver_override_brake` it reaches 3.85 m/s^2 of
    deceleration while `BrkReq_mps2` is exactly 0, because that is the driver braking and
    not the ACC. Restricting to the requirement's own `system_states` and to a released
    brake pedal drops that run's worst 2 s average from 3.85 to 0.03 m/s^2. Without the
    gate a check reports failures the ACC never caused.
    """
    status = trace.on_grid("ACC_Status", t_grid)
    gate = np.isin(status, np.asarray(allowed_states, dtype=float))
    if require_brake_released:
        gate &= trace.on_grid("DrvBrkPedal_Pct", t_grid) <= PEDAL_RELEASED_PCT
    if require_accel_released:
        gate &= trace.on_grid("DrvAccPedal_Pct", t_grid) <= PEDAL_RELEASED_PCT
    return gate


def masked_moving_average(
    values: np.ndarray, gate: np.ndarray, window_samples: int
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Mean of `values` over every window of `window_samples` lying fully inside `gate`.

    Returns `(start_indices, means)` for the admitted windows only.

    A window that straddles the edge of the gated region is dropped, not partially
    averaged. Averaging it would quietly mix in samples from outside the requirement's
    scope -- for a 2 s window at 100 Hz that is up to 199 out-of-scope samples diluting
    one in-scope sample, which can turn a real violation into a pass or the reverse.
    """
    count = int(window_samples)
    if count <= 0 or values.size < count:
        return np.empty(0, dtype=int), np.empty(0, dtype=float)
    value_sum = np.concatenate(([0.0], np.cumsum(values, dtype=float)))
    gate_sum = np.concatenate(([0], np.cumsum(gate.astype(np.int64))))
    starts = np.arange(values.size - count + 1)
    fully_inside = (gate_sum[starts + count] - gate_sum[starts]) == count
    starts = starts[fully_inside]
    means = (value_sum[starts + count] - value_sum[starts]) / count
    return starts, means


def rising_edges(flag: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Indices where a 0/1 flag becomes asserted. The first sample counts if it is 1."""
    asserted = flag > 0.5
    previous = np.concatenate(([False], asserted[:-1]))
    return np.flatnonzero(asserted & ~previous)


def find_episodes(condition: np.ndarray, t_grid: np.ndarray) -> list[Episode]:
    """Every contiguous run of samples for which `condition` is True."""
    held = np.asarray(condition, dtype=bool)
    if not held.any():
        return []
    previous = np.concatenate(([False], held[:-1]))
    following = np.concatenate((held[1:], [False]))
    starts = np.flatnonzero(held & ~previous)
    ends = np.flatnonzero(held & ~following)
    return [
        Episode(int(first), int(last), float(t_grid[first]), float(t_grid[last]))
        for first, last in zip(starts, ends, strict=True)
    ]


def first_index_where(condition: np.ndarray, at_or_after: int) -> int | None:
    """Index of the first True at or after `at_or_after`, or None if there is none."""
    hits = np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(condition, dtype=bool)[at_or_after:])
    return int(hits[0]) + at_or_after if hits.size else None


def measure_latency(
    t_grid: np.ndarray, condition: np.ndarray, reference_t: float, search_from: int
) -> LatencyMeasurement:
    """Latency from `reference_t` to the first sample at or after `search_from` satisfying it.

    `reference_t` and `search_from` are separate on purpose. ACC-SYS-SAF-021 measures from a
    detection instant 500 ms into a sensor dropout but has to start searching at the beginning
    of the dropout, so that a system reacting before the debounce elapses is seen and reported
    as early rather than missed.
    """
    hit = first_index_where(condition, search_from)
    return LatencyMeasurement(
        reference_t=reference_t,
        reached_t=None if hit is None else float(t_grid[hit]),
        trace_end_t=float(t_grid[-1]),
    )


def status_name(value: float) -> str:
    """Human name for an `ACC_Status` sample, or the raw number if it is not a known state."""
    try:
        return AccStatus(int(value)).name
    except ValueError:
        return f"unknown({int(value)})"


def require_channels(trace: Trace, names: Iterable[str]) -> None:
    """Raise `MissingSignalError` for the first channel that is absent.

    Called before any measurement, so that a file lacking a measurand reports
    INCONCLUSIVE naming the channel instead of measuring whatever it does contain.
    """
    for name in names:
        if not trace.has(name):
            raise MissingSignalError(name)


def run_check(spec: CheckSpec, path: Path, evaluate: Callable[[Trace], Verdict]) -> Verdict:
    """Uniform wrapper: open the trace, apply the shared INCONCLUSIVE rules, evaluate.

    Every check module's `run()` is this call and nothing else, so all nine behave
    identically on an unreadable file, a missing channel or a truncated collision run.
    """
    try:
        with open_trace(path) as trace:
            if trace.is_collision_run:
                contact = trace.collision_t_s
                moment = f"{contact:.2f} s" if contact is not None else "an unrecorded time"
                return spec.inconclusive(
                    path,
                    f"run {trace.run_id} ended at a collision at t = {moment} and the file is "
                    "truncated there, so it is not valid evidence for this requirement",
                )
            require_channels(trace, spec.signals)
            return evaluate(trace)
    except TraceError as exc:
        return spec.inconclusive(path, str(exc))

for the two SAF checks on commanded deceleration, but it is *not* this requirement's
measurand either: it is limited to -3.500 in every run by limiter stage L2, whereas the
achieved value adds drag and rolling resistance on top of the commanded brake and so runs
deeper. This requirement is written on the achieved value, and on the achieved value the
